narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 91% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. That high failure estimate triggered the rejection, though it is a prediction, not a certainty about your ability.

The most influential factor was your third-year class-rank decile: it was 1.00, compared with an average of about 5.79 among accepted students, and it pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second most important factor was your first-year class-rank decile, also 1.00 versus an accepted average of about 6.00, which also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.10, compared with an accepted average of 3.23, was the third factor and worked slightly in your favor by pushing toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the two class-rank signals.

What you should do next is request a human review of your file, explain any context behind your class-rank results, and ask what evidence would support a successful reapplication. Consider retaking the LSAT if you can improve your score, consult an admissions adviser, and reapply after strengthening your academic record or providing a clear plan for bar-exam preparation.
